images.title: Koch Snowflake: 3 sides become 12
images.purpose: Shows the bump rule turning a triangle into a six pointed star, so the side count is multiplied by 4.
images.composition: Plain white background with generous empty margins; the main object is large and centred and fills about 60 percent of the frame; nothing else is drawn. Two shapes side by side, same height, left and right of centre, joined by one bold amber arrow. Step name above each, side count below each.
images.exact_structure: Left: an equilateral triangle, point up, outlined thick teal #0072B2, side 9 units (3 sides). Right: the Step 1 shape made from the same triangle: each side is cut into 3 equal thirds and an equilateral bump is raised outward on the middle third, with the middle third removed; the result is a six pointed star with exactly 12 equal outer sides, each 3 units, outlined thick teal; the 3 bumps are filled light amber #E69F00 so the new parts stand out, the rest of the star is white. Bold amber arrow between them with '× 4' on it. Above: 'Step 0', 'Step 1'. Below: '3 sides', '12 sides'.
rejection: any count of objects, cells, ticks or rows that differs from the numbers stated in the spec
any text beyond the listed visible text, or any listed text misspelled or altered

images.takeaway: Every side becomes 4 sides, each one third as long, so 3 sides become 12.
images.description: Shows the bump rule turning a triangle into a six pointed star, so the side count is multiplied by 4.
images.context: Concept T4.C3; one image that shows only the main idea.
images.teaching_notes: Step 2 would have 48 sides; left out to keep the picture clear. Perimeter goes 3 to 4 for side 1 unit.

image_decisions.why: A practice concept with no tool; the image fixes the bump rule and the multiply by 4 count.
